surprise.title: The guns of World War I fell silent at 6 AM on your clock, 108 years ago
surprise.body: The armistice that ended the fighting in World War I was agreed around 5 AM on November 11, 1918, in Marshal Ferdinand Foch's private railway carriage in the Compiègne Forest north of Paris, and it took effect at 11:00 AM Paris time. France kept Greenwich time back then, so that famous eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month lands at 6:00 AM in Tallahassee, nearly an hour before today's 6:59 sunrise. The United States marked it as Armistice Day until 1954, when veteran organizations pushed to rename it Veterans Day so it would honor everyone who has served. Tallahassee keeps the eleventh-hour tradition alive this morning: the parade steps off down Monroe Street at 10:40 AM, with the 11th Hour Ceremony at the Vietnam Memorial and a festival in the Park Avenue parks afterward. The timing is kind, too, because the late morning is the clearest stretch of the day, around 70°F with almost no clouds at 11 AM before the sky clouds over after noon.
